embedded.title: Run rusthinq in Home Assistant
embedded.description: Home Assistant downloads and runs the rusthinq daemon, which LG ThinQ appliances connect to on this host. Appliances open HTTPS on port 443; if another port is used here, redirect 443 to it.

data_description.https_port: Where appliances are provisioned and register (443 unless a redirect points here)
data_description.mqtt_port: Announced to appliances when they register; any free port works

migrate.title: Move an existing rusthinq into Home Assistant
migrate.description: Keeps the CA your appliances trust, their device records, the LG account and the settings appliances notice, so nothing needs provisioning again. Where should the backup come from?

menu_options.migrate_fetch: Copy it from the running rusthinq

migrate_fetch.title: Copy from the running rusthinq
migrate_fetch.description: Home Assistant downloads the backup from the old rusthinq's management API (rusthinq 0.2.0 or later). rusthinq hands it out only when its management API has a user and password or listens on loopback only, since it holds the CA key and LG tokens.

data_description.url: Base URL of the old rusthinq's management API, for example http://192.168.1.10:44401

migrate_upload.title: Upload a backup
migrate_upload.description:
Take a backup on the old host with the dashboard (System → Download backup) or `sudo thinqctl backup`, and upload it here.

Without either, archive config.toml with the files it names, in its directory, for example:
`tar czf rusthinq-export.tar.gz config.toml ca.key ca.cert devices.json account.json account.json.pairings`

data_description.archive: rusthinq-backup-….tar, or a .tar.gz of config.toml and the files it names

migrate_confirm.title: Move this rusthinq in
migrate_confirm.description:
The backup holds:
- host name: **{hostname}**
- devices: **{devices}**
- LG account: **{account}**
- written by rusthinq {rusthinq} at {created}

Existing files that differ from this backup: **{conflicts}**
Overwriting the CA may mean provisioning appliances again. Only files included in the backup are replaced; files absent from it are kept.

1. **Stop rusthinq on the old host now**, and keep it stopped: both would answer the same appliances and LG account.
2. Check the ports, filled in with the old installation's, and submit.
3. Point the appliances' route (DNS or redirect) at this host.

data.overwrite_existing: Overwrite conflicting files included in the backup

data_description.https_port: Where appliances are provisioned and register (443 unless a redirect points here)
data_description.mqtt_port: Announced to appliances when they register; any free port works

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the management API.
error.invalid_auth: The management API rejected the username or password.
error.duplicate_ports: Each listener needs its own port.
error.overwrite_required: Select the confirmation box to overwrite. Files not included in the backup will not be deleted.
error.backup_unsupported: This rusthinq cannot hand out a backup (it needs 0.2.0 or later). Upload a file instead.
error.source_running: The old rusthinq at {problems} still answers. Stop it first.

ports_unavailable.title: rusthinq cannot open its ports
ports_unavailable.description:
The built-in rusthinq cannot start: {problems}.

Free the port, or choose other ports by removing the integration and adding it again (the CA and devices stay in /config/rusthinq, so nothing is lost). Appliances always open HTTPS on 443; if rusthinq listens elsewhere, redirect 443 to it. rusthinq keeps retrying on its own.

init.title: LG account
init.description:
rusthinq is {state}. Last error: {error}.

The LG account lets rusthinq name your appliances and keep the LG ThinQ app working through its per-device bridge.

menu_options.refresh: Sign in again with the saved credentials

login.title: Sign in to LG
login.description: rusthinq asks LG for a sign-in page for this country.

data_description.country: Two-letter country code of the LG account, e.g. KR or US

login_complete.title: Sign in to LG
login_complete.description:
1. Open [LG's sign-in page]({sign_in_url}) and sign in.
2. The browser ends on a blank page whose address starts with https://…/login/iabClose. Copy that whole address.
3. Paste it here.

logout.title: Sign out of LG
logout.description: rusthinq forgets the LG credentials. Bridged devices disconnect from LG until you sign in again; local control is unaffected.

reset.title: Reset rusthinq data
reset.description: This removes the CA, device records, LG account, retained topics, and saved daemon settings. Appliances may need to be provisioned again. Download a backup first if you may need this data.

data.confirm_reset: I understand; erase rusthinq data and create a new CA

error.reset_required: Select the confirmation box to reset rusthinq.

abort.no_bridge: This rusthinq has no LG bridge.
abort.reset_failed: rusthinq could not be restarted after reset.

not_connected.message: rusthinq is not reachable right now; try again once it is.

device_online.message: {name} is connected to rusthinq and would come right back. Switch it off or take it off the network first, then delete it.
